samples.summary: Merge-map resource cap moved out of the atomic `doc.update`; the queued write is applied unconditionally at flush (TOCTOU on a DoS guard)
samples.evidence: The merge budget (`MaxMergeEntries`/`MaxMergeCoveredCells`, documented in packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:8-42 as the guard against "a document nobody can open again") used to be evaluated *inside* the queued update closure, against the live CRDT root at commit time (old `applyMerge`). After this delta the check runs at call time (yorkie-store.ts:1014-1021) against `projectedMerges()`, while the closure pushed at :1034 writes `ws.merges[sref]` unconditionally when `endBatch` flushes (:1247-1268). Between the two there are many awaits (e.g. `mergeSelection` awaits a `store.get` per covered cell, `applyPasteMerges` awaits `clearCellsUnderMerge`/`buildDependantsMap`/`calculate`), during which a remote collaborator's merge additions can be applied to the document. The flushed map can therefore land above the cap that the store is advertised (yorkie-store.ts:994-1000) as the floor for, and a worksheet over the cap is also permanently un-replaceable through `PUT /merges`, which validates the whole body (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:117-166). Overshoot is bounded by the blocks the batch itself queued, and exploitability depends on a macrotask (network apply) interleaving a mostly-microtask await chain, hence medium confidence / minor severity.

samples.summary: `batchMerges?.set(...)` fails open: if the overlay map is ever absent while `batchOps` is set, every batched merge is budgeted against the same starting map
samples.evidence: `setMerge` (line 1033) and `deleteMerge` (line 1048) record the batch's pending merge writes through optional chaining on `this.batchMerges`. The budget check at :1014-1021 is only correct within a batch because that overlay exists; if `batchMerges` is null while `batchOps` is non-null, each queued block is admitted against the identical on-disk map, so N blocks that individually fit are all accepted and flushed together — an unbounded overrun of `MaxMergeEntries`/`MaxMergeCoveredCells` in a single update, i.e. exactly the unopenable-worksheet condition the cap exists to prevent. Today only `beginBatch` (:1229-1233) sets `batchOps`, and it always sets `batchMerges` too, so the state is unreachable — but the guard is written to degrade silently rather than to fail closed (a nested `beginBatch`, or any future code path that populates `batchOps` alone, re-opens it with no visible symptom). Prefer a non-optional access / invariant assert so a missing overlay is loud.

samples.summary: `projectedMerges` ignores queued `shiftCells`/`moveCells` ops that rewrite the whole merge map at flush, so the cap can be spent against stale spans
samples.evidence: `projectedMerges()` (yorkie-store.ts:975-991) composes the document's current `merges` with `batchMerges` only. Batched `shiftCells`/`moveCells` are pushed as opaque closures (:497-498, :529-530) that recompute `ws.merges` wholesale at flush time via `shiftMergeMap`/`moveMergeMap`. `shiftMerge` grows a span when rows/columns are inserted inside a block (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:134-137: `if (index <= end) return [start, end + count]`), so a batch that mixes a structural shift with `setMerge` budgets the new block against pre-shift spans and can flush a map whose `coveredCells` exceeds `MaxMergeCoveredCells` — the load-time `rebuildMergeCoverMap` cost the cap bounds. Low confidence that a single batch mixes both today; reported because the new budget guard reads as covering the whole flushed map when it does not. (Overlaps the correctness lens' finding on the same line; raised here for the resource-exhaustion impact.)

samples.summary: The merge cap on the CRDT path is enforced only in the browser; the doc comment calls the client store "the floor", but no server-side check bounds a merges map pushed through Yorkie
samples.evidence: yorkie-store.ts:994-1000 (and docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:147-170) describe `YorkieStore.setMerge` as the floor under the path that reaches the CRDT directly. That floor is client code: a modified client, or a script driving the Yorkie SDK with a legitimate `rw` token, can write `root.sheets[tab].merges` with any number of entries/spans. The only server-side merge validation is `parseMerges` on the v1 `PUT /merges` body (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:117-166) and the structural helpers in packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:155,192; the Yorkie auth webhook (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts) authorizes the verb, not the document content. One writer with edit access can therefore plant a merge map whose `rebuildMergeCoverMap` walk makes the worksheet unopenable for every other collaborator — a persistent, cross-user DoS that the three new client-side budget spends in this delta cannot prevent. Not introduced by this change, but the change is what advertises the client check as an enforcement boundary; worth stating explicitly so the cap is not mistaken for one.
